content:
The condition is that no run of three consecutive empty chairs exists.

Let \(E\) be the number of empty chairs and \(O=N\) be occupied chairs. Since each run of empty chairs has length at most \(2\), and each run must be separated by at least one occupied chair, we get
\[
E \le 2O.
\]
Also \(E+O=60\), so
\[
60-O \le 2O \implies O \ge 20.
\]
This is achievable by repeating the pattern \(O,O,E,E\)? Actually pattern \(1,0,0\) repeated gives 20 occupied and 40 empty chairs, with no three consecutive empty chairs.

Thus the smallest possible \(N\) is
\[
\boxed{20}.
\]
